title: Strengthening Support and Dignity for Migrant Domestic Workers and Singapore Families
what_it_is: Strengthening Support and Dignity for Migrant Domestic Workers and Singapore Families

sections.label: Migrant domestic worker numbers
sections.summary: Singapore has more than 308,000 migrant domestic workers, up from about 247,000 five years ago.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Caregiving is not a single chapter in life.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: And holding that cycle together are more than 308,000 migrant domestic workers (MDWs) in Singapore today, up from about 247,000 just five years ago.

sections.label: Households with elderly residents
sections.summary: In 2024, Singapore had 1.46 million households and 27% had at least one resident aged 65 and above.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: In 2024, Singapore had 1.46 million households and 27% had at least one resident aged 65 and above.

sections.label: Caregivers Training Grant expansion
sections.summary: The ask is to expand the Caregivers Training Grant to include advanced home care and language training.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Yet, many MDWs still arrive trained mainly for chores.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: And this is why my first ask is this: the Caregivers Training Grant has provided excellent support for families with eldercare needs by affordably training helpers to take on caregiving duties.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: My ask is to expand the Caregivers Training Grant to include advanced home care as well as language training, particularly in Mandarin, Malay, Hokkien, Cantonese and other dialects, which are useful for eldercare.

sections.label: Employment agency standards
sections.summary: The second ask is to raise professional standards for employment agencies, especially in complex care households.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: A good, responsible employment agency makes all the difference.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: So, my second ask is this: raise professional standards for employment agencies, especially in handling complex care households.

sections.label: Primary Care Plan for MDWs
sections.summary: The third ask is to extend a Primary Care Plan-type scheme to migrant domestic workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: A wrong match does not just only cost money; it can break a family and deeply hurt our workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: I propose enhanced training and accreditation pathways for employment agencies focused on caregiving assessment, counselling skills and individual agents to empower trade associations to reward and recognise agencies that demonstrate lower transfer rates and better post-placement outcomes, and create a stronger feedback loop between families, MDWs, employment agencies as well as Government agencies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: So, my third ask is this: to extend a Primary Care Plan (PCP)-type scheme to our MDWs.

sections.label: MDW hospitalisation insurance limit
sections.summary: The current basic insurance of $60,000 annual limit for a MDW's hospitalisation might not cover severe cases.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Similarly, the current basic insurance of $60,000 annual limit for the hospitalisation of a MDW might not cover more severe cases, leaving our employers responsible for the excess and payment.

sections.label: Mental health support framework ask
sections.summary: Calls for mental health screening and counselling in a national MDW support framework, with resources for social and recreational activities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: These programmes and safety nets – social clubs, craft workshops, excursions, counselling – help build community and resilience.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: So, my fourth ask is to make mental health screening and counselling part of a national MDW support framework, should the need arise, and to provide resources to scale up such social and recreational activities.

sections.label: Part-time MDW care pathways
sections.summary: Asks for regulated, care-focused part-time MDWs and home care pathways, since the ecosystem leans on live-in helpers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: The current ecosystem leans very heavily on the live-in helper model, which works well for many but not for all.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: So, my fifth ask is to develop regulated, care-focused part-time MDWs and home care pathways.

sections.label: Levy and subsidy eligibility review
sections.summary: Asks to review levy and subsidy eligibility to reflect real dependency rather than just age.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Currently, the $60 concessionary levy is available for households with a child below 16 years or an adult above 67 years old.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: There are gaps in the current levy framework.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: So, my final ask is this: review levy and subsidy eligibility to reflect real dependency, not just age.

sections.label: CTG enhancement from April 2024
sections.summary: The CTG was enhanced from 1 April 2024, rising from $200 to $400 per year per care recipient.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: The CTG was enhanced from 1 April 2024, increasing from $200 to $400 per year, per care recipient.

sections.label: HSS companies increase
sections.summary: Since the HSS became a permanent scheme in 2021, HSS companies grew from about 80 to 240.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: Since formalising the HSS as a permanent scheme in 2021, the number of HSS companies has increased from about 80 to 240 today.

sections.label: HCG and levy enhancements
sections.summary: MOH will raise HCG monthly payout to up to $600 and PCHI threshold to $4,800, with a $60 concessionary levy rate.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Health has announced that it will enhance HCG by first increasing the monthly payout from up to $400 per month to up to $600 per month; and raising the per capita household income (PCHI) eligibility threshold, from $3,600 to $4,800.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: Second, to support families with greater need for MDWs, local households with caregiving needs enjoy a concessionary levy rate of $60 per month, instead of $300.

sections.label: Minimum annual claim limit increase
sections.summary: The minimum annual claim limit rose to $60,000 in 2023 from $15,000 before 2023, covering 99% of MDW inpatient and day surgery bills in public healthcare institutions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: The minimum annual claim limit was raised to $60,000 in 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: This was a significant increase from $15,000 prior to 2023, and covers 99% of inpatient and day surgery bills incurred by MDWs in the public healthcare institutions.

sections.label: Employers using employment agencies
sections.summary: More than 80% of employers hire their MDWs with the help of an employment agency.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: Today, more than 80% of employers hire their MDWs with the help of an employment agency.

sections.label: Employment agency guidelines and penalties
sections.summary: Employment agencies should not mislead, give inaccurate information or pressure clients; breaches bring demerit points, possibly suspending or revoking the licence.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: For instance, employment agencies should not mislead, or provide inaccurate information to their clients, or provide undue pressure on their clients. employment agencies found to have breached these guidelines will be issued with demerit points, which may result in the eventual suspension or revocation of the employment agency licence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Pursuant to Standing Order 2(3)(a), I wish to inform hon Members that the Sitting tomorrow will commence at 12.30 pm.
